skill.name: set-up-shopware-meta-new-customer-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up Meta bidding signals for first paid orders in a Shopware 6 sales channel. Verify revenue or profit events before selecting a custom conversion in Meta.
skill.summary: Set up and verify Meta conversion signals for first paid Shopware orders.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown formatting, vendor documentation, or routine setup checks. Confirmed risks include writes without a clear approval step, access to order details, unpinned installation, and instructions to collect an access token. The setup can also enable broader tracking than requested and point profit bidding at the wrong event.

remediation.issue: The assistant is told to request a Meta Conversions API token.
remediation.suggestion: Require direct token entry in the Product Metrics app or an approved secret field. Remove all directions to pass the token through chat or as a shell argument.

remediation.issue: Product Metrics writes and retries lack a consistent approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Show the workspace, storefront, destination, and proposed change before each write. Obtain approval and verify that each retry matches the approved change.

remediation.issue: Routine classification checks can put order details in the assistant session.
remediation.suggestion: Use a test order or request only the fields needed to classify orders. Report aggregate counts and omit customer identifiers and individual margins.

remediation.issue: The installation example does not pin the installer or skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and distribute a verified artifact from the audited commit. Keep installation separate from task execution.

remediation.issue: New customer setup can activate a broader Shopware-to-Meta data flow.
remediation.suggestion: Before enabling live sending, show the merchant the destination, event types, customer fields, and consent requirements. Ask for explicit approval of the full scope.

remediation.issue: The main skill gives the all-order profit event as a new customer bidding example.
remediation.suggestion: Use PMNewCustomerProfit with CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT for first-order profit. Validate the event and purpose together against a first-order test before recommending a campaign change.

semantic_findings.title: Meta Access Token Requested by the Assistant
semantic_findings.description: The Meta guide says to enter the token in the app, but also says, "An assistant must ask you for it." The main skill exempts Meta tokens from its secret rule and tells the assistant to pass the token to a command. That can expose the credential in conversation or tool records.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both files explicitly tell the assistant to handle a real access token. The review found no evidence of a leaked token or a dedicated secret entry mechanism.

semantic_findings.title: First-Order Setup Can Enable Broader Live Tracking
semantic_findings.description: The setup for first-order bidding directs the merchant to leave Meta sending enabled. The destination also sends cart, checkout, and other purchase events, with matching fields and IP addresses when consent permits. The bidding checklist does not ask the merchant to approve that broader data flow separately.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The destination setup and event table show the broader scope. The merchant enables it in the app, and the documentation describes consent controls.

semantic_findings.title: General Profit Event Suggested for New Customer Bidding
semantic_findings.description: The main skill names PMOrderProfit with ORDER_PROFIT for profit bidding, but the first-order guide requires PMNewCustomerProfit with CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT. Following the main example can steer optimization toward paid orders from returning customers as well.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files name different events and purpose rules, and the Meta guide describes PMOrderProfit without a first-order restriction.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Bidding for New Shopware Customers
content.value_statement: A standard purchase conversion does not distinguish new Shopware customers from returning buyers. Use Product Metrics to verify a first-order signal and select the matching conversion in Meta.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status using its CLI or MCP when connected.
Guide pairing of one Shopware sales channel and connection of a Meta pixel or dataset.
Check whether recent paid orders are classified as new, returning, or unknown.
Explain which first-order event and purpose rule to use for revenue or profit.
Guide verification of test event delivery before the merchant selects an ad set conversion.
limitations: Setup requires a Product Metrics Pro workspace, a compatible Shopware 6.7 installation, and access to the Meta destination.
Customer history is scoped to the paired sales channel, and past orders are not sent to Meta as new events.
Custom events require marketing and analytics consent. The profit signal needs complete margin data.
The merchant creates the Meta custom conversion and selects it in the ad set. Later refunds do not revise sent events.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Confirm that the correct Shopware sales channel is paired and a test purchase can reach the intended Meta destination.

use_cases.title: Configure an Acquisition Campaign
use_cases.description: Choose a first-order revenue or profit signal and verify it before selecting a custom conversion for one ad set.

use_cases.title: Investigate Customer Classification
use_cases.description: Check whether sales channel scope or paid order history explains unexpected counts of new, returning, or unknown orders.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what I need to use first-order bidding for my Shopware store in Meta. Do not connect accounts or change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Review Installation Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the setup status for [workspace] and [sales channel]. Identify missing steps without changing settings or requesting credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Test Purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: Help verify that a paid test order from [sales channel] appears as a new customer revenue event in Meta. Do not display customer identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Review Profit Bidding Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: preparing one ad set for first-order profit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether [sales channel] has complete margin data and a verified first-order profit event. Give me the Meta conversion rule and leave the ad set unchanged.

output_examples.input: Check what is missing before I create the Meta custom conversion.
output: The Shopware sales channel is active and linked to the intended property.
The first-order event has not arrived in Meta yet.
Place a paid test order with marketing and analytics consent, then check Test events in Events Manager.

output_examples.input: Which event should I use for first-order profit?
output: Use PMNewCustomerProfit with the purpose set to CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT.
Choose Purchase as the category and use the event's value and currency.
Confirm that a first-order test event includes profit before you select the conversion in your ad set.

best_practices: Confirm the sales channel, Meta destination, event scope, and consent settings before enabling live tracking.
Enter credentials directly in the appropriate app, not in an assistant chat.
Verify a paid test order from a new customer before changing the conversion used by one ad set.
anti_patterns: Using the general order profit event when the goal is first-order profit.
Assuming a buyer is new across all storefronts because they are new to one sales channel.
Leaving the test event code active when you expect events to count in reporting.

faq.question: What counts as a new customer?
faq.answer: A customer is new if their account or guest email has no earlier paid order in that sales channel.

faq.question: Why is the event missing from the Meta selector?
faq.answer: Meta lists the event only after receiving it. Use a paid first-order test with marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: Can I optimize on profit instead of revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the first-order profit event once margin data is complete. A loss-making first order sends a value of zero.

faq.question: Will Product Metrics backfill past orders into Meta?
faq.answer: No. It sends events after tracking goes live, and Meta rejects events more than seven days old.

faq.question: Where should I enter the Meta access token?
faq.answer: Enter it in the Product Metrics app when adding the Meta destination. Do not paste it into an assistant conversation.

faq.question: Will the assistant change my Meta campaign?
faq.answer: No. You create the custom conversion in Meta Events Manager and select it as the ad set conversion event.
